text.p: Sergio Marchionne, named chief executive of Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG as of next April, said the forecast for 1996 net profit to exceed that of 1995 still held true.
Marchionne also told Reuters in an interview that his personal view was that aluminium prices would be restored to a level above $1,500 per ton by the end of 1996 or the beginning of 1997.

"Our statement at the beginning of the year that this year's results would exceed 1995 results is still true," Marchionne said, adding: "It is undoubtedly true the movements in prices of aluminium have an impact on earnings this year, but it would be improper at this stage to analyse that further."
In 1995 Alusuisse's group net profit rose 86 percent to 385 million Swiss francs and at its 1996 half-year news conference the company said it was confident 1996 results would exceed those of 1995.
Marchionne also said it was premature to deal with the issue of changes to Alusuisse's parent strategy or financial targets.
In the medium- to long-term Marchionne said the market consensus was that current aluminium prices were not sustainable.
"We are now feeding off the bottom of the barrel in terms of the aluminium cost structure," Marchionne said.
Prices between $1,650 to $1,850 were more sustainable, he added.
"I think there will be a restoration of prices above $1,500 at the end of the year or beginning of 1997," he added.
During 1997 aluminium prices could then gradually move up to a level around $1,650, he said, characterising his own prediction as a "courageous statement".
Marchionne acknowledged the recent movements of aluminium prices would have an effect on earnings, but it was too early to analyse the effect.

Aluminum prices have remained stable above support around $1,400 per tonne where any dips have been finding consumer demand, although upside gains have been slow to materialise amid profit-taking and possible producer liquidation.
Currently, three-month delivery London Metal Exchange aluminium is trading around $1,430 per tonne. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
